subject: SKU portability exceptions and co-sell coverage for APAC launch
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SKU portability exceptions and co-sell coverage for APAC launch

Team —

Acme Analytics (prospect) is moving toward an APAC pilot and they pushed back on a single cross-cloud SKU. Their legal/regulatory folks called out data residency and audit log requirements for AU/SG and a separate China validation window (they may end up using a partner-managed option for CN). We need to decide which SKUs we list per cloud and what exceptions we make in regions where co-sell/marketplace rules or compliance block a canonical option.

Quick context: attached is our current SKU matrix (SKU_matrix_v3.xlsx) plus notes from Acme’s compliance team (APAC_compliance_notes.pdf). High-level asks from Acme:
- A lightweight entry SKU for hosted (cloud-managed) for APAC except CN
- A dedicated/reserved SKU for customers needing audit logs + onshore data storage in AU
- Clear lead-time estimates for Marketplace listing approvals (AWS/GCP/Azure) per SKU

Questions for this thread:
1) Which SKU variants can we realistically list across AWS / Azure / GCP for APAC day 1?
2) Where do we need to carve exceptions (CN, TW, AU) and what alternative SKUs do we propose?
3) Co-sell readiness: which cloud needs extra artifacts (certs, attestation) to unlock the program?

Please review attachments and reply with a concise recommendation. I want a decision we can present to Acme by EOD Friday.

Thanks —
Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Sr. Partner Manager, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com

Attachments: SKU_matrix_v3.xlsx, APAC_compliance_notes.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 11:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SKU portability exceptions and co-sell coverage for APAC launch

Rafael / everyone —

Quick read-through: good summary. My recommended mapping (short):
- redwood-hosted-entry (lightweight): list on AWS + GCP in APAC regions (SG, SIN, AU-syd). Azure listing OK for global program but note: Azure co-sell in Greater China requires a partner managed flow and separate legal review.
- redwood-dedicated-compliant: list on AWS Marketplace (private offer) and Azure Marketplace (managed application) where we can guarantee onshore logging + KMS control. GCP has a Marketplace path but requires additional attestation for data residency — slower.

Exceptions:
- CN: do not list standard hosted SKU. Recommend partner-managed on-prem / private-deployment SKU (redwood-private-cn) and route co-sell via our channel partner in CN.
- TW: treat like APAC but confirm local tax paperwork; no technical SKU change expected.
- AU: dedicated customers want SOC and audit-log proofs; propose dedicated SKU plus an add-on for extended audit retention (addon-audit-365).

Operational notes:
- Need marketplace listing IDs and product packages for each cloud. I’ll start drafting the AWS private offer package but we will need NA/legal signoff for Azure CN exceptions.
- Timeline: if we run parallel listing submissions, AWS/GCP can be 3–5 weeks; Azure could be 5–8 weeks depending on co-sell enablement and paperwork.

I attached a simple mapping into a new tab of SKU_matrix_v3.xlsx (see my inline comments).

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Cloud Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SKU portability exceptions and co-sell coverage for APAC launch

All —

Agree with Karthik’s mapping. A couple product/GTN constraints to call out so we don’t overpromise:
- Entry SKU should default to a lower compute profile and a short-term SLA for the pilot. We should not enable aggressive batching/quant modes by default for the APAC hosted entry (cost + latency concerns).
- The dedicated SKU needs to offer a clear boundary: customer-managed KMS + audit log export to their storage (S3/Azure Blob/GCS) + daily export for AU customers. That’s the compliance ask — we can deliver but it’s an engineering scope.

Suggested pricing tiers (names only): redwood-core (entry), redwood-core-plus (higher throughput), redwood-dedicated-compliant (reserved). We can finalize numbers after Ben confirms GTM pricing guidance.

I uploaded a short co-sell enablement doc to the drive and attached as co-sell_playbook_v2.docx. That doc lists the artifacts each cloud wants to see for co-sell certification (SOC2, data flow diagram, audit log examples).

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Director, GTM Strategy — Redwood Inference

Attachment: co-sell_playbook_v2.docx
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SKU portability exceptions and co-sell coverage for APAC launch

Folks —

This is workable but Acme’s procurement team has an internal mandate: they want one SKU per consumption model where possible (hosted vs dedicated) to simplify billing across subsidiaries. If we force many cloud-specific SKUs they will push back.

Ask Rafael: can you surface to Acme legal that the dedicated SKU includes the audit retention addon (addon-audit-365) and that onboarding time for a dedicated/private deployment is ~8–10 weeks from PO? They will need that for their procurement checklist.

HubSpot: I added notes to the deal (see link). Also we should prepare a simple one-page co-sell brief for Azure; they are stricter about partner evidence. Naomi — can you author a one-pager by Thu EOD?

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Sales, Enterprise — Redwood Inference

Related link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/8491
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme-analytics.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 13:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SKU portability exceptions and co-sell coverage for APAC launch

Rafael / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side after internal review:
- Procurement is comfortable with two SKUs (hosted vs dedicated) as long as the dedicated SKU includes the audit retention add-on and a signed attestation for AU data residency.
- For China: we cannot use the hosted SKU. We are open to your partner-managed option for CN.
- Lead times: we need approximate timelines to present to our board. AWS private offer + GCP listing is acceptable if each is ~4 weeks; Azure timeline will be a gating question for our procurement legal.

Please supply a simple table with: SKU name, cloud availability, expected listing lead time, and compliance notes. That will help us finalize the PO.

Sanjay Rao
VP, Infrastructure — Acme Analytics
Sanjay.Rao@acme-analytics.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme-analytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SKU portability exceptions and co-sell coverage for APAC launch — Decision + next steps

Sanjay / team —

Thanks — summary and actions below (decisions we’ll present to Acme):
1) SKU decision (day 1 APAC):
   - redwood-core (hosted entry): list on AWS (ap-southeast-1), GCP (asia-southeast1). Azure listing submitted but Azure co-sell may require extra attestation and may be delayed for CN/PRC customers.
   - redwood-dedicated-compliant (reserved): AWS private offer + Azure managed listing where allowed. GCP listing path supported but flagged as slower due to attestation.
2) Exceptions:
   - CN: use partner-managed redwood-private-cn (no standard hosted listing).
   - AU: dedicated-compliant must include addon-audit-365; engineering to provide daily export and KMS control.
3) Timeline estimates (ballpark):
   - AWS: 3–5 weeks for private offer;
   - GCP: 4–6 weeks;
   - Azure: 5–8 weeks (attestation + co-sell enablement may extend timeline).

Action owners & deadlines:
- Rafael: send the SKU table (SKU | cloud availability | lead time | compliance notes) to Acme by Mon 2026-04-19.
- Naomi: deliver one-page Azure co-sell brief by Thu 2026-04-16 (thx for the doc draft).
- Karthik: start AWS package and add marketplace product IDs by 2026-04-23.
- Engineering (cc: Lauren): confirm audit-log export and KMS path for AU dedicated by 2026-04-24.

Attachments for Acme: SKU_matrix_v3.xlsx (updated mapping), co-sell_playbook_v2.docx, APAC_compliance_notes.pdf. I’ve linked the HubSpot deal and Drive folder with artifacts.

If no objections, I’ll send this summary to Sanjay as the formal decision note and ask for PO timing.

Best —
Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Sr. Partner Manager, Redwood Inference
